notes.783: 786: the star 'born after the ancient Arcadians' is the Moon, subject of 787–794. 791: 'tractari!' as printed; the exclamation mark seems a misprint.

nodes.text: the wanton goddesses of the groves,
the Dryads who pursue the mountain-roaming Pans;
or, looking down on you from the star-bearing sky,
the star born after the ancient Arcadians
will not be able to guide her white chariot.
Lately, too, she reddened, though no dingy
cloud stood in the way of her bright face;
but we, troubled by the darkened goddess,
thinking she was being dragged down by Thessalian spells,
raised a clanging: you had been the trouble,
you the cause of delay; while the goddess of nights
gazes at you, she has held back her swift course.
May the cold harass this face more sparingly,
may this face seek the sun more rarely:
